newsitem.title: USA: Uruguay buys Venezuelan asphaltic crude for Feb.
newsitem.headline: Uruguay buys Venezuelan asphaltic crude for Feb.

text.p: Uruguay's state-owned oil company ANCAP bought asphaltic crude for delivery February 12-14 in a private spot transaction with Venezuela, trade sources said Friday.
ANCAP bought BCF-24 crude from Lagoven, a unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela, they said.
The cargo of around 500,000 barrels will load between January 30 and February 2, they said.
Traders speculated that ANCAP paid around $5.00 a barrel under benchmark West Texas Intermediate for the cargo.
Uruguay normally buys around one million barrels a year of such crude for asphalt, and has previously bought heavy Saudi and Iranian crudes, traders said.

Separately, ANCAP has postponed the shutdown of the La Teja refinery to around mid-February to mid- to late March. The facility was originally supposed to have been shut down for repairs later this month, company officials said.
